gate: Experience wants to come out as a story. That is the felt shape of this code, a low pressure to turn what was lived into something tellable, to find the angle that makes the listener lean in. A person carrying this gate notices the narrative inside an ordinary day before anyone asks for one. The trip to the market becomes a small tale on the way home. The argument becomes a scene with its own timing. Stimulation is the word the system uses, and it is accurate, because the drive here is to keep the field interesting, to keep the listener awake. The misread is to call this performance or showing off. It is not. The code is doing its actual work when it turns raw experience into a shape that another person can step inside. Without that translation, the experience stays private and stops there. With it, the experience becomes something shared.
centre_field: Of all the places in the body-map, the throat is the loudest. Every other current in the chart is moving toward it, looking for a way out. The throat is the exit point, the moment where inner motion becomes outer act. For this code to land here, in the broadcast centre, is the whole teaching. Storytelling is not a flourish on top of thinking. It is the manifestation gesture itself, the way an idea actually leaves the body and enters the room. When this gate fires, something inner is being shaped into voice, and the listener gets a piece of experience they could not have had on their own. There is also a cost wired into the placement. The throat is the burnout site of the chart. A storyteller who talks past their own timing, who broadcasts without pause, will exhaust the very instrument they need. The teaching is to honour the silences as part of the song.
channel: Storytelling without an idea to carry is just noise dressed up. This code reaches up through the body toward the gate of ideas, and the two together form the channel of curiosity. The reach matters in a specific direction. Ideas alone stay abstract, suspended in the mind, never quite touching anyone. The story is what gives an idea legs, a setting, a person inside it the listener can identify with. Stimulation needs something to be about. Without that upstream feed of concept and pattern, the storyteller starts narrating thin material and feels the dissatisfaction of it. Without the downstream exit through this gate, the idea stays in someone's head and never finds an audience. The channel is the loop where concept becomes narrative, narrative sparks new concept, and the cycle keeps feeding itself. This code lacks the source on its own. It is a mouth waiting for something worth saying.
